subject: R/qtl genetic map construction: errors in pull.rf and formLinkageGroups() function

messages.author: a8334d46c5367a85
messages.subject: R/qtl genetic map construction: errors in pull.rf and formLinkageGroups() function
parts:
Good morning Dr. Broman,

I hope you are coping as well as you can in these tough times. I have a couple of questions regarding the R/qtl genetic map construction.


I am creating a linkage map of the F2 population from WGS data. I have ~70,000 SNPs across 12 chromosomes, and one of the chromosome has ~20,000 SNPs.

I have been trying to handle this dataset in two ways:

  • 1.       Read data of each chromosome separately and Create linkage groups (ideally 1) for that chromosome. This approach can handle this dataset. But I cannot find any literature using this approach. Can the result obtained by this process be trusted?

I tested this approach with array genotyped dataset of ~751 markers and when pushing all chromosomes at once, the result shows a large first linkage group which has markers from other chromosomes( which seems wrong to me) and I know from the input data that first chromosome has fewer SNPs than another chromosome; whereas when processing data separately for each chromosome, I get a much accurate picture and the markers aren’t mixed across the chromosome. Why isn’t this approach used more frequently? What am I missing?

 

 

  • 2.       Read all 12 chromosomes data altogether, it gives error like :

“Error in rep(0, n.mar * n.mar) : invalid 'times' argument
In addition: Warning message:
In n.mar * n.mar : NAs produced by integer overflow”

 

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rqtl-disc/XlpNTOz-E7s

here you have mentioned that “There's no strict limit on the number of markers, but there are a number of functions that won't work well with very large data sets.”

 

I get above mentioned error in pull.rf() and formLinkageGroups() function

 

Have you updated any part of the code/function for handling a huge dataset?


Thanks,

Prashant

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] R/qtl genetic map construction: errors in pull.rf and formLinkageGroups() function
parts:
est.rf() estimates the recombination fraction between all pairs of markers, and the way that formLinkageGroups() was written requires that you do so. But this limits the number of markers that you can reasonably use with these functions. The only way around this is to work with a smaller subset of your markers.

But if you know which markers are on which chromosomes, it is not clear to me why you would want to try to form linkage groups.

karl

parts:
During variant calling, I called variants of each chromosome separately. 

I already have SNPs separated by chromosome; does that mean I can clean up the dataset of each chromosome separately and consider them as linkage groups without the use of formLinkageGroups() ?
The reason I am trying to push all 12 chromosomes at once is - if I just push each chromosome separately pairwise comparison will be limited to that particular chromosome. And at rf=0.35 and lod=6 criteria in formLinkageGroups() a couple of chromosome splits into multiple linkage groups (e.g. linkage group 1 = markers from 0-80 Mbp positions; linkage group 2 = 81-end of the chromosome) with a distinct gap in between linkage groups. I was hoping if I push all 12 chromosomes at once, I might get a better composition of 12 distinct linkage groups and then I could remove misplaced markers based on the information I already have.

With such high-dimensional data, you'll need to find other procedures to identify problems in the data.

If you have information about what chromosomes markers are on and their order and physical positions along the chromosomes, I would look to see whether there are markers that seem out of place, rather than trying to establish chromosomes and marker order from scratch.

karl
